quandoUsar: Secondary actions on an object the person is already looking at, like a file, a card, or a project, opened with a right-click on the object itself.
Surfaces that should not show a menu button, but whose actions must remain reachable by keyboard (`Shift + F10` or the menu key).
quandoEvitar: Use `dropdown-menu` when the actions need a visible trigger or separators between groups; this menu is a flat list opened over the object.
Avoid on objects that already respond to clicks, like links, cards that open, or selectable rows: a simple click or tap anywhere on the target also opens the menu.
Use `swipe-actions` when each list row's actions should appear with a swipe gesture on touch.

teclado.acao: With focus on the target, open the menu just below it, with focus on the first enabled item.
Move through the enabled items and wrap around at the ends.
Go to the first and last enabled item.
Select the focused item, close the menu, and return focus to the target.
With focus in the menu, closes it and returns focus to the target.

acessibilidade: The target is a `<div>` with `tabIndex=0`, `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`, and `aria-label`; the menu is `role="menu"`, with `role="menuitem"` items, and gets the same `label` (default in English, “Context menu”).

On open, focus goes to the first enabled item, but the menu does not trap focus: `Tab` leaves it without closing it and, with focus outside, `Esc` no longer closes it (only a tap outside or scrolling).
`checked` does not become `aria-checked` and only draws a checkmark when the item has no `icon`; the state does not reach the screen reader.
movimento: The menu grows from the click point (the origin stays at the pointer even when the menu is pushed into the screen) on a short spring, and leaves fading faster than it entered.
Items enter in sequence, 35 ms apart, and a single highlight slides between rows under the pointer; with the keyboard, it jumps straight to the focused item.
With “reduce motion”, the menu only fades, items appear with no sequence, and the highlight does not slide.
responsivo: The menu uses `position: fixed` and is pushed to stay 8 px from the window edges; above 300 px in height (or the screen height) it scrolls inside, and long labels end in an ellipsis.
It closes when the page scrolls or the window is resized, instead of following the target.
notasIA: Wrap the object: `<ContextMenu label="Ações do arquivo" items={itens}>…</ContextMenu>`; the target becomes a block `<div>`, and each item needs `id` and `label`, with the action in `onSelect`.
Give every item an `icon`: without one an ellipsis icon appears, and `checked` only swaps that icon for a checkmark; `destructive` paints the item with the danger color.
Do not put links or buttons inside the target expecting them to work on their own: the click on them bubbles up to the target and also opens the menu.
